issues.description: Duplicate 'transcriber_error' entry in the message_type tuple
issues.detail: The error-type tuple lists 'transcriber_error' twice. Both reviewers flag this as sloppy and as a symptom of a missing named ADT/frozenset for the error contract. Lift the set of error message_types to a named constant or Enum so it is de-duplicated, testable, and stateable.

issues.description: Collapsed 'Error:' prefix silently weakens push_error's observable contract
issues.detail: The previous code emitted typed prefixes ('Auth error:', 'Quota exceeded:'); the new code uses a single generic 'Error:'. Downstream consumers grepping on those prefixes break silently and observers can no longer distinguish error class without re-parsing. Either restore typed prefixes or pass message_type as a structured field.

issues.description: Removing the outer try/except deletes the disconnect breadcrumb with no replacement
issues.detail: The fix correctly stops swallowing disconnects so the reconnect loop works, but the old 'WebSocket connection closed' log line is gone. Log once at warning before re-raising, and document the new contract ('returns iff clean close; raises on transport error') in the docstring so a future subtype does not re-introduce the swallow.

issues.description: Inner 'except Exception' inside the async-for can still mask transport errors
issues.detail: The remaining broad except inside the message loop will catch transport-level exceptions raised mid-iteration alongside JSON/handler errors. Narrow it to handler-domain exceptions, or re-raise after logging if the exception did not originate from _process_response, to preserve the 'raise on disconnect' contract this PR establishes.

issues.description: No test covers the disconnect path or the expanded error types
issues.detail: The core claim of the fix ('the process used to hang; now it does not') has no regression test. A small unit test that feeds a disconnect into the iterator and asserts the coroutine returns/raises would have caught the original bug and will catch the regression when somebody re-wraps this in a try/except later.
changelog/3233.fixed.md ends without a newline. Trivial, but every tool that concatenates these files for release-notes assembly produces garbage. Add the newline to match codebase convention.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR fixes a real bug: the outer try/except in _receive_messages was swallowing websocket disconnects and defeating the reconnect loop. Deleting it is correct. Execution is sloppy: 'transcriber_error' is listed twice in the error-type tuple (a missing named ADT), the collapse to a generic 'Error:' prefix silently weakens push_error's observable contract relative to the old typed prefixes, and the disconnect log line is gone with no replacement. The remaining inner broad except can still mask transport errors, and there is no test for the disconnect path. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — restore/structure the error contract, log once before re-raising, narrow the inner except, add a disconnect test, and fix the trailing newline.
